title: Holtec Pioneer 2 (SMR-300 at Palisades): Pre-Acceptance Regulatory Audit Plan for the Palisades SMR, LLC Pioneer Units 1 and 2 Construction Permit Application [['Audit Plan']]

documents.text:
November 6, 2026

    PRE-ACCEPTANCE REGULATORY AUDIT PLAN FOR THE PALISADES SMR, LLC
          PIONEER UNITS 1 AND 2 CONSTRUCTION PERMIT APPLICATION
                          (EPID NO. L-2026-LRM-0140)

                                  APPLICANT INFORMATION

Applicant:                               Palisades SMR, LLC

Applicant Address:                       Holtec Technology Campus
                                         One Holtec Blvd
                                         Camden, NJ 08104

Facility Name:                           Pioneer Units 1 and 2

Docket No.:                              99902049

Background:

By letter dated September 30, 2026 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management
System (ADAMS) Package Accession No. ML26273A416), SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades
SMR, LLC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holtec International (collectively, Holtec) submitted a
construction permit application for a power reactor pursuant to Title 10 of the Code of Federal
Regulations (10 CFR) Part 50, “Domestic Licensing of Production and Utilization Facilities,” to
the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) for review. The facility, Pioneer Units 1 and 2,
would be constructed and operated near Covert, Michigan. The construction permit application is
currently undergoing an acceptance review to determine if the application contains the required
scope, level of detail, and regulatory information needed to begin a full technical safety and
environmental review. This regulatory audit is intended to assist the NRC staff in its acceptance
review.

Purpose:

The purpose of the audit is for the NRC staff to gain a better understanding of the
completeness and technical sufficiency of the Pioneer Units 1 and 2 construction permit
application by providing an opportunity to review and discuss the contents of the preliminary
safety analysis report (PSAR) and proposed exemptions. The audit is expected to facilitate the
completion of the acceptance review by allowing the NRC staff to review and discuss the PSAR
and proposed exemption contents in an expedited fashion with applicant staff. If the NRC staff
identifies information that is needed for completeness and technical sufficiency, Holtec will be
notified.

Regulatory Audit Basis:

The basis for this regulatory audit includes the following key regulations and guidance relevant
to the NRC staff’s review:

   •   Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 2.101(a)(2) requires the NRC
       staff to review applications submitted under 10 CFR Part 50 for completeness and
      acceptability for docketing.
   • 10 CFR 50.34, “Contents of applications; technical information,” provides the
      requirements for the contents of a construction permit application.
    • Regulatory Guide 1.70, “Standard Format and Content of Safety Analysis Reports for
       Nuclear Power Plants,” (ML0111340072) provides applicants the standard format and
       content for safety analysis reports submitted to the NRC review, which includes the
       PSAR that is reviewed for construction permit applications.
    • NUREG-0800, “Standard Review Plan for the Review of Safety Analysis Reports for
       Nuclear Power Plants: [Light-Water Reactor] (LWR) Edition” (SRP) provides guidance
       for the NRC staff on conducting a review of light water reactor safety analysis reports.
    • DNRL-ISG-2022-01, “Safety Review of Light-Water Power Reactor Construction
       Permit Applications” (ML22189A099) is NRC staff guidance used to facilitate the safety
       review of light-water power reactor construction permit applications and supplements
       NUREG-0800

Regulatory Audit Scope:

The audit scope is the review of the Pioneer Units 1 and 2 PSAR and proposed exemptions.
Administrative information for this audit, such as the exact technical topics to be discussed, will
be identified in subsequent correspondence, such as an email, and dates will be proposed for
audit meetings where a full discussion of the information will be held.

Information and Other Material Necessary for the Regulatory Audit:

Holtec should be prepared to provide documents, reports, calculations, and other supporting
material, as applicable, related to the PSAR and proposed exemptions in a timely manner. The
NRC staff may request that Holtec make these materials available in the online reference portal.

Safety Audit Team:

Michael Orenak                    Lead Project Manager
Mihaela Biro                      Lead Technical Reviewer
Sean Piela                        Technical Reviewer
JS Nie                            Technical Reviewer
George Thomas                     Technical Reviewer
Syed Haider                       Technical Reviewer
Ed Stutzcage                      Technical Reviewer
Raul Hernandez                    Technical Reviewer
Joseph Staudenmeier               Technical Reviewer

Additional audit team members will be added, as needed.

Audit Logistics:

Entrance Meeting: November 10, 2026 (tentative)

Exit Meeting: TBD

Audit meetings will take place mainly in a virtual format, using Microsoft Teams, or via other,
similar platform. Audit meetings will be scheduled on an as needed basis after the entrance
meeting and, as appropriate, once the NRC staff has the opportunity to review any documents
placed in the online reference portal. The audit will begin with the entrance meeting and
continue as necessary, with activities occurring intermittently during the audit period.

The audit period will be determined depending on the progress made by the NRC staff and
 Holtec in addressing audit items. Audit items will be shared with Holtec via the NRC’s External
Collaboration SharePoint site.

The NRC staff requests that all documents in the audit scope be provided by Holtec on an
online reference portal established by Holtec. Use of the online reference portal is acceptable
provided that Holtec implements measures to limit access to specific NRC staff (e.g., based on
NRC e-mail addresses or the use of passwords that will only be assigned to the NRC staff
directly involved in the audit on a need to‑know basis) and to make the documents view-only
(i.e., prevent NRC staff from saving, copying, downloading, or printing any documents). The
conditions associated with the online reference portal must be maintained throughout the audit
process. The NRC staff who should initially be granted access to the portal are listed in the
“Team Assignments” section of this audit plan. The NRC project managers for the audit will
provide Holtec with the names of additional NRC staff who should be granted access when
needed.

The audit will be closed via discussion during the last audit meeting or through an email from
the NRC project manager to the submitter after the last audit meeting.

Special Requests:

None

Deliverables:

At the completion of the audit, the audit team will issue an audit summary within 30 days after
the exit meeting but will strive for a shorter duration. The audit summary will be publicly
available in ADAMS.
